answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small deposit that stays locked while it trades, like a lantern that only stays lit while fuel remains. New accounts start with a crystal-clear reputation ledger: every completed job leaves a public echo of verified work, and peers weight that history before trusting a stranger. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real stake per identity plus the time to build genuine history, while one honest agent earns trust cheaply through a single verifiable record.
